aria: Animated recap of the Nuggets' 133 to 124 home win over the Rockets: Jamal Murray's 17-foot jumper with 3:51 left that put Denver up 116 to 115, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Nikola Jokić's 26 points and 11 assists, the top scorers, how the Nuggets won, and Sunday's game at Chicago.
notes: Box score from the Denver Nuggets' 133–124 home win over the Houston Rockets on Nov 20, 2026. The full box score pages (CBS Sports, Covers.com) could not be opened for this run, so the player lines are put together from written game coverage: Denver's from Fadeaway World's player ratings, checked against NBC Sports, the Colorado Springs Gazette and DenverSports; Houston's from NBC Sports, Roundtable and the AP. All 133 Denver points are accounted for player by player, and the Denver lines add up to the reported team totals (field goals 47 of 86, threes 13 of 30, free throws 26 of 28, 36 assists, 36 rebounds, 37 bench points). Houston's starters account for 112 points and its bench for 12 (AP), so all 124 are accounted for, but not every Houston bench line was found. The quarter scores (31–31–37–34 to 33–27–42–22, from sportpreferred and JKN, checked against DenverSports and the Gazette) add up to both totals: 62–60 Denver at the half and 102–99 Houston after three. Points in the paint (54–62) and fast-break points (15–6) are from Sport News Africa, and the Gazette gives the same margins; rebounds (36–39), bench points and second-chance points are from DenverSports; Houston's 23 of 35 free throws is from the Houston Chronicle ("missed 12 of 35"). The biggest leads (Denver 12, Houston 5) are from Yardbarker and the AP. Records are from the game stories (the site's standings were not yet updated when this was built).

The game had 32 lead changes and 17 ties, and neither team led by more than 5 until 2:01 remained (AP). Nikola Jokić had 2 points at halftime and 18 in the third quarter on 8 of 9 shooting (Nuggets On SI), when Houston scored 42 on 76.2% shooting, the most Denver has allowed in a quarter this season (DenverSports). Fred VanVleet's 20-footer made it 115–110 Houston with 5:10 left (AP), then Denver scored 10 straight in 1:55 and closed on a 23–9 run (AP). Jamal Murray's jumper at 3:51 put Denver ahead 116–115 (DenverSports), and Christian Braun's steal and dunk out of a Houston timeout made it 120–115 (DenverSports). Denver made all 15 of its fourth-quarter free throws (DenverSports). Alperen Şengün had 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists, his second triple-double of the season (AP), and VanVleet scored a season-high 25 (NBC Sports). Denver has won 6 of its last 8 (AP); Houston won the first meeting 110–100 on Nov 9, so the season series is 1–1 (AP). The Nuggets play at Chicago on Sunday and the Rockets host the Clippers on Monday (Plain Text Sports schedule; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Jamal Murray's jumper with 3:51 left that put Denver ahead 116–115 (DenverSports gives the clock, the score and a 17-foot pull-up; Haberci TV gives the same clock and score; the AP's 10 straight Denver points from 115–110 put the score before it at 115–114). It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up jumper. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Denver Nuggets or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Murray's listed 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds with No. 27 (RealGM), with his arms scaled to a reported 6-foot-7 wingspan (CraftedNBA), in Denver's home white. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
